findings.message: This host did not provide a verified exact author model for the planning review.

I found no errors in the 12 scenario blocks (17 compiled cases), so I'm approving. Every scenario sits under the numbered Rule it proves, uses a valid persona (SWM), carries the one affected surface tag (@surface.safeword-cli), runs through the real CLI, and stays inside out_of_scope and the project and milestone non-goals. The out_of_scope field was supplied and readable. The ticket declares no parent, so no inherited scope applies. Each rejection has a positive sibling, so an implementation that always returns one fixed answer would fail the suite. The demo scenario proves success. The fresh-input rows of the R4 freshness table prove that a genuine observation still verifies. The internal input variations are assigned to named lower-level test matrices in dimensions.md. I have three warnings, none blocking. The demo scenario proves only part of the Killer Demo Payoff. One distinct recovery path (accepted scope changed before a run) is covered only by a lower-level test. R5 checks the execution-evidence-only label on successful observations, not on refused ones.

Killer Demo proof is partial. The Payoff says one observation produces verifiable evidence 'while the historical ledger remains visibly unfinished and no completion authority is granted'. The @demo scenario 'Complete fixed-lane execution produces verifiable current evidence' only checks the observation's contents and the retained report. It never runs verification and never checks that the ledger is unchanged or that no completion authority is granted. Those claims are proved separately by the R4 freshness rows that still count as current and by the R5 scenario, so no Rule is left uncovered. To make the demo scenario cover the whole Payoff, add a Then saying the observation is labelled execution-evidence-only and the 33 deferred identities and ledger stay unchanged. Alternatively, record a skip noting that R5 carries that part.

R1 has a distinct recovery path with no acceptance scenario. R1 says a changed accepted scope must be refused before execution. dimensions.md says the recovery here differs from the dirty-input case: the maintainer must request review of an updated shipped contract, because rerunning the old contract cannot fix it. That path has only the lower-level proof in observer-source-identity. The R4 outline row for a scope edit covers a similar recovery, but only at verification time, after a successful observation already exists. If the pre-execution check is wired wrongly, the CLI could tell the maintainer to commit or clean when it should ask for contract review, and the acceptance scenarios would still pass. Consider an R1 rejection scenario, or make the lower-level matrix explicitly assert this recovery message through the real CLI entry point.

R5 says 'Both successful and refused observations identify their execution-evidence-only meaning', but the only R5 scenario uses a successful observation. dimensions.md assigns refused and interrupted outcomes to observer-history-preservation and observer-recovery-messages, so a lower-level proof is named. That is acceptable, but the plan should make sure those matrices assert the execution-evidence-only label on refusals, not just that historical files are unchanged. A do-nothing refusal leaves files unchanged anyway, so that check alone proves nothing.

R2's required-result outline is well formed. Its three rows (absent from the report, skipped, failed) vary only the required assertion's outcome and expect the same refusal. Runner exit failure is a different mechanism and correctly has its own scenario. Duplicate or ambiguous results and malformed reports are left to named lower-level matrices.

The R4 freshness outline pairs two input changes that remove current success (assertion source, accepted scope) with two that keep it (Work Log append, non-input audit output). An implementation that always says 'stale' or always says 'current' fails the outline either way. The retained-evidence-readable check applies to every row.

The R3 retry scenario now starts from a saved non-empty failure diagnostic and requires it to be byte-identical afterwards and still not verify as success. This fixes the earlier finding that the retention check passed trivially. The mid-run candidate-change scenario adds an explicit check that a commit change during the run blocks success, closing the gap reported by the earlier quality review.
